methodological_rigor.justification: This is a single-institution, retrospective, single-arm case series of 15 patients (18 lesions) with heterogeneous gynecological malignancies, heterogeneous systemic therapies, variable prescriptions (30-50 Gy in 5-10 fractions), and no comparator group. The authors acknowledge that planning was individualized rather than protocolized. Median follow-up is only 4.67 months (range 0.73-20.10 months), which is too short for 12-month survival estimates beyond exploratory Kaplan-Meier. Cumulative dose assessment for re-irradiation uses a simplified worst-case EQD2 summation without deformable registration. Statistical treatment is limited to descriptive statistics and Kaplan-Meier with patient-at-risk counts; no confidence intervals are reported in the main results text, no multivariable analysis, no competing-risks treatment for local control.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Case series corresponds to Oxford LoE 4. Clinical relevance is moderate because the population (heavily pretreated pelvic-abdominal recurrent/metastatic gynecological cancers including 80% prior radiotherapy) has few options and the MR-Linac adaptive workflow is a technology of growing interest. Findings (73.3% ORR, 92.3% 6-month LC, one grade 3 enteric fistula) are clinically suggestive but too small to inform practice beyond hypothesis generation.

reporting_quality.justification: Reporting is structured with explicit inclusion/exclusion criteria, ethics approval (National Cancer Center/Cancer Hospital 25/221-5167), CTCAE v5.0 and RECIST v1.1 definitions, clearly defined endpoints, and supplementary tables for treatment parameters and systemic therapy. STROBE is not explicitly cited; no flow diagram is provided; the '[REDACTED]' placeholder for the prescriber remains in Section 2.3. Data availability is weak with no statement or deposited materials. For a feasibility/toxicity study with a prediction-adjacent claim, either STROBE or a bespoke cohort reporting format would apply; STROBE is the closest fit.

novelty_literature.justification: MR-Linac adaptive SBRT for gynecological malignancies has prior published feasibility data (refs 9, 21, 22), so the novelty here is a focused single-institution case series in heavily pretreated pelvic-abdominal recurrent/metastatic disease combined with diverse systemic agents. The combination of re-irradiation, adaptive workflow, and systemic therapy in this specific subpopulation is a meaningful incremental extension but not a fundamentally new approach or first report.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is organized with standard IMRaD structure, clear subsections for planning and adaptive workflow, and useful supplementary tables. Figures (Kaplan-Meier, waterfall plot) are referenced. Weaknesses include a residual '[REDACTED]' placeholder in Section 2.3, occasional imprecise phrasing ('systemic metastases' for 'metastatic disease'), and a mismatch between the abstract grade 3 enteric fistula and the description of 'severe late toxicity'. Tables and figures would benefit from integrated 95% CIs.

key_strengths: Real-world, technically detailed description of MR-Linac adapt-to-shape workflow (utilized in 65% of fractions; median 45 min session) in a heavily pretreated population
Clinically meaningful endpoints reported (6-month LC 92.3%, ORR 73.3%) with patient-at-risk counts on Kaplan-Meier estimates
Transparent acknowledgment of individualized rather than protocolized planning, short follow-up, and single-arm design as limitations
Defined OAR constraints and conservative re-irradiation dose summation approach described in detail
key_concerns: Very small heterogeneous cohort (n=15, 18 lesions; mixed histologies and diverse systemic agents) precludes robust efficacy or safety inference
Median follow-up of 4.67 months makes 12-month OS/PFS/LC estimates highly unstable and late toxicity detection inadequate
Non-protocolized individualized planning and simplified worst-case EQD2 summation without deformable registration limit reproducibility and dosimetric accuracy
Residual '[REDACTED]' placeholder in Methods Section 2.3 indicates unresolved manuscript redaction
No data availability statement or code/data deposit; no CIs around key time-to-event estimates
chief_reviewer.rationale: A heterogeneous feasibility case series with interesting but preliminary results; Tier 4 is the realistic ceiling, and major revisions are needed to tighten reporting, complete redactions, and add confidence intervals with longer follow-up.
